answer: A verifiable delay gate makes each identity prove one hour of sequential computation before its weight accrues: the work cannot be split across machines, so every fake pays its own unshareable hour. Each identity crosses a dune of 3,600 sequential hash steps, each step depending on the last. A pearl grows one layer per 10 minutes of that work, and only a fully layered pearl earns weight. A juniper cutting planted at enrollment must add one measured centimeter of growth during the delay hour, so 100 fakes need 100 hours and 100 cuttings.
